approach: Find the angle of the velocity above the incline surface, then use the same along- and perpendicular-to-incline equations as launching up a slope.

steps.text: The velocity is 45° above the horizontal reference line, and the incline is 30° above horizontal, so the velocity is 15° above the incline surface.
Resolve the initial velocity along the incline and perpendicular to it using this 15° angle.
steps.equation: along the incline: 20√2 cos15°; perpendicular to it: 20√2 sin15°

steps.text: The particle lands back on the incline when the perpendicular displacement returns to zero; solve for the time using the perpendicular part of gravity.
Find the along-incline displacement at this time for the range.
State the results; this is the final answer.

final_answer.value: time of flight ≈ 1.69 s, range along the incline ≈ 39.04 m

common_mistakes.text: Using the full 45° as the angle from the incline, instead of subtracting the 30° incline angle first, gives a wrong time of about 4.62 s.
